title: TXT Records Serve SPF, DKIM, and Separate Verification Checks

cover.subtitle: Keep each record tied to its service.
cover.visual: Three small cards for SPF, DKIM and Verification, each with a distinct icon and no DNS values.

sections.name: 01-match-each-txt-record-to-a-named-consumer
sections.heading: Each TXT record serves a named consumer
sections.scene: Three separate TXT envelopes at apex, selector._domainkey, and verification name lead to three distinct service readers. Use labels TXT, SPF, DKIM, Verify only.
sections.alt: Each TXT record serves a named consumer.

sections.name: 02-maintain-one-valid-spf-policy-for-each-sending-identity
sections.heading: Each sending identity needs one valid SPF policy
sections.scene: Two SPF policy cards marked conflict collapse into one policy connected to two authorized mail senders. Keep unrelated verification TXT separate.
sections.alt: Each sending identity needs one valid SPF policy.

sections.name: 03-publish-dkim-keys-at-the-selector-that-signs-mail
sections.heading: DKIM retrieves the public key through a selector
sections.scene: A signed message shows d=example.com and s=selector1 pointing to selector1._domainkey.example.com, where a public key answers. Private key stays at sender.
sections.alt: DKIM retrieves the public key through a selector.

sections.name: 04-verify-service-challenges-and-remove-records-deliberately
sections.heading: Service verification requires deliberate publication and retirement
sections.scene: A requested verification token travels from service account to exact DNS name, then a checker confirms it. A retired service exits through a deliberate review gate.
sections.alt: Service verification requires deliberate publication and retirement.

purpose: Initial illustration plan. The final image review manifest records actual asset hashes and visual revisions.
